summary: This PR introduces a new `parentMode: 'hand-fk'` weapon proxy mode for the Meshy character rig, which parents the synthetic weapon bone directly to the right-hand FK bone instead of the model root. It also updates the `gripLocalPosition` oracle in the Meshy weapon attachment profile and adds a standalone trace/verification tool. The runtime logic changes are small and targeted; the main risks are a semantic offset-space mismatch, a dead function in the new test tool, and a fragile `--compare` assertion invariant. No CI checks are configured for this repo.
perspectives_used: Foreman: implementation sequencing, null-safety, and variable-scope verification
Gasket/Auditor: contradiction detection, failure modes, and test assertion correctness

findings.issue: `modelLocalOffset` added in hand-local space despite its name implying model space
findings.impact: In `hand-fk` mode the weapon bone is a child of `rightHand`, so all position offsets are in hand-local space. Adding `modelLocalOffset` (which is named and documented as a model-space correction) in this local frame will produce incorrect placement whenever the hand is not at the model origin or is rotated. The profile currently sets `modelLocalOffset: [-0.11512, 0.00773, -0.01127]`, which was tuned for the two-hand-center world-space path and will produce a different result in hand-local space.
findings.evidence: New block at diff line +3897: `if (Array.isArray(proxy.config.modelLocalOffset)) proxy.root.position.add(new THREE.Vector3().fromArray(proxy.config.modelLocalOffset));` — the bone is parented to `rightHand` (line +3863), so this offset is applied in hand-local coordinates, not model/world coordinates as the field name implies. The existing two-hand-center path applies `modelLocalOffset` after converting to world space via `this.model.updateMatrixWorld(true)` and explicit world-to-local transforms.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) rename the field to `handLocalOffset2` / `handExtraOffset` to make the space explicit, (b) document clearly that in `hand-fk` mode both `handLocalOffset` and `modelLocalOffset` are summed in hand-local space, or (c) transform `modelLocalOffset` from model space to hand-local space before adding it, consistent with how the two-hand-center path handles it.

findings.issue: `worldPosition` helper function is defined but never called
findings.impact: Dead code increases maintenance surface and may confuse future readers into thinking it is part of the verification logic. It is not exercised by any assertion in the file.
findings.evidence: Lines 52-55 define `function worldPosition(THREE, node) { ... }`. A search of the rest of the file finds no call site for `worldPosition`. The actual world-position work is done inline via `sabreMesh.localToWorld(...)` and `localPointFromWorld(...)`.
findings.recommendation: Remove the unused `worldPosition` function, or use it in place of the inline `localToWorld` calls to reduce duplication.

findings.issue: `--compare` mode asserts that the baseline and current MUST differ, making the test fail if run twice against the same output
findings.impact: If a developer captures a baseline and then immediately runs `--compare` against it (or if the profile values are unchanged), the assertion `assert(payload.comparison.numericallyChangedFromBaseline, 'offline main vs salvage did not numerically change at profile gripLocalPosition')` will throw. This is an unusual invariant for a regression test and will produce confusing failures in CI or iterative development.
findings.evidence: Lines 173-179: `payload.comparison = { ..., numericallyChangedFromBaseline: !arrayClose(current, previous) }; assert(payload.comparison.numericallyChangedFromBaseline, 'offline main vs salvage did not numerically change at profile gripLocalPosition');`
findings.recommendation: Reconsider the assertion direction. A regression test should assert that the current value matches the baseline (i.e., `assert(!numericallyChangedFromBaseline, ...)`), or the `--compare` flag should be documented as a 'verify change was applied' mode with a clear comment explaining why divergence is required.

findings.issue: `rightHand.updateMatrixWorld(true)` is called after `localToWorld` operations that depend on up-to-date world matrices
findings.impact: The `sabreMesh.localToWorld(gripLocal.clone())` and `sabreMesh.localToWorld(tipLocal.clone())` calls at lines 148-149 require `sabreMesh`'s world matrix to be current. `rightHand.updateMatrixWorld(true)` is called at line 155, after these operations. If the scene graph has not been updated before the `localToWorld` calls, the computed world positions may be stale. In practice `rightHand.updateMatrixWorld(true)` is called at line 130 before `weaponGrip` is added, so the matrices may be stale after the `add` calls.
findings.evidence: Line 130: `rightHand.updateMatrixWorld(true)` — called before `rightHand.add(weaponGrip)`. Lines 133-145: `weaponGrip` and `sabreMesh` are added and configured. Lines 148-149: `sabreMesh.localToWorld(...)` called without an intervening `updateMatrixWorld`. Line 155: `rightHand.updateMatrixWorld(true)` called after the fact.
findings.recommendation: Move `rightHand.updateMatrixWorld(true)` to immediately before the `localToWorld` calls (after all scene-graph mutations are complete), or call it once after all `add`/`position`/`quaternion` mutations and before any world-space queries.

test_gaps: No automated test verifies the runtime behavior of `parentMode: 'hand-fk'` in `pose-lab.js` itself — the new trace tool only validates the profile data and a simplified offline scene graph, not the actual `buildWeaponProxy` / `updateWeaponProxy` code paths.

The existing `test_meshy_pose_parity_arm_contract.mjs` contract does not assert anything about `parentMode: 'hand-fk'` or the new update branch, so a regression in the new code path would not be caught by that contract.
No test covers the interaction between `parentMode: 'hand-fk'` and `animatedSocketRotation` being truthy (i.e., when a clip animates the WeaponGrip quaternion track while in hand-fk mode).
non_postable_concerns: No CI checks are configured for this repository (list_ci_checks returned 0 check runs). There is no automated gate preventing regressions from merging.

The `pose-lab.js` file is very large (~3900+ lines) and was truncated by the read tool; the exact definition site and scope of `animatedSocketRotation` in the update function could not be directly verified from source. The existing test contract (`test_meshy_pose_parity_arm_contract.mjs`) asserts `js.includes('if (!animatedSocketRotation)')`, confirming the variable exists in the file, but its declaration relative to the new `hand-fk` block could not be confirmed line-by-line.

The `gripLocalPosition` change from `[0.6535, -0.02302, -0.07317]` to `[0.69507, -0.02421, -0.06231]` is a tuning/calibration change. Its correctness depends on the physical sabre model geometry and cannot be verified through static analysis alone.
